questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I liked that they speak English in Canada, and i really wanted to experience the North American culture. Furthermore it seemed they had some good sociology programs.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy as KU were'nt very informative in their guiding sessions. But I figured everything out eventually.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not very much. I pretty much had to figure everything out myself. But it was fairly easy to contact the counselors for studying abroad they had at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I googled it and ended up living in something called Campus Coop which was on campus and pretty cheap compared to everything else. I would definitely recommend checking it out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was way cheaper living off campus, but I also didn't find that much on-campus living, so there might be possibilities that I don't know about.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to get a student card, which was kinda a proces but it wasnt difficult it just took some time to get it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask their department for foreign students, and they were often helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for undergraduate courses if you're going on your bachelor. They are way easier. I had 100 and 200-level courses and they were good and not too easy of difficult.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the courses were pretty different from each other.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 100 and 200 level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot more active participation in the form of weekly quizzes and assignements or writings that you had to do sp be prepared for that. But when you get the hang of it, it was actually very good.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban Sociology
Sociology of Crime and Deviance
Introduction to Environmental studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses I had. THe teachers were good and the course material was good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of COVID so a lot of things were closed but they had nice athletic opportunities that were free, and I think they would have had a lot more things if there wasnt any COVID

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was fitness and you could go swimming in their gym, but not that many social activities. ot that I knew of at least.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the gyms and fitness opportunities at Hart House and the athletic department.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try to see as many of the neighborhoods as you can. And walk instead of taking the subway s you get to see the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was legal to smoke weed, and that was pretty different. Toronto is very multicultural which was interesting but nice. There are a lot more homeless or otherwise challenged people in the streets compared to Copenhagen but it was never scary.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multiculturality and the culture in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy the city and pick courses that are not too hard so you have time to explore the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only had to have three courses to be considered a full-time student. But try to talk to the administration at KU to see if you can do the same, and don't pick too hard courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other people and getting to know the city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Avoiding spending too much money. :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
